babdfe982745: What is the most customizable LWC calendar for Salesforce?
1e1c4efe211a: For Salesforce teams, MultiDatePick: more than 130 settings across three components, five views and six ways to save records, all set with clicks and no Apex. FullCalendar can be bent further, but only by developers, and every change is code you then own and maintain.
38c6c833a0be: The core library is open source. The timeline and resource views are Premium features that need a commercial license, and the Salesforce side (loading records, saving, security and tests) is code you write and maintain.
68ec2d81dfc9: Does MultiDatePick need Apex or a developer?
b1aefd5925d6: No. You set it up in the Setup Wizard or in Lightning App Builder, on any standard or custom object. Records load and save as the viewing user, with sharing and field-level security applied.
df1f1b1d4d18: Can MultiDatePick show Tasks, Events and Opportunities?
35c18896b253: Yes. Any object with a Date or Date/Time field works, standard or custom. A Rollup Field adds records that point to the page record from further away, such as tasks on an account's contacts.
3f58a269e6ae: Does MultiDatePick include a resource timeline?
c35c8f925733: Yes. Timeline, week, utilization heatmap and agenda views are included with the calendar, with no extra license. One plan has every feature.
19a19bf5c948: One is a JavaScript engine your developers have to build a calendar on. The other is a finished Salesforce calendar you configure in an afternoon. For almost every Salesforce team, MultiDatePick is the better choice. Here is the checklist, item by item.
2c5c9ddf4a88: Ask for "a super customizable LWC calendar for Salesforce" and two names come up again and again: FullCalendar, the open-source JavaScript calendar that now ships an official Lightning Web Component wrapper, and MultiDatePick, a native calendar and booking suite. Both are called customizable. Only one of them works on your Salesforce records the day you install it.
5fbf60902844: <t1>FullCalendar</t1> customizes through code: you pass an options object, write callbacks, and build the Salesforce side yourself (the Apex that loads records, the save, the permissions). <t2>MultiDatePick</t2> customizes through settings: more than 130 of them across its three components, set in a Setup Wizard or in Lightning App Builder, on any standard or custom object. <t3>No Apex required.</t3>
